reason: Research (limited WebSearch, nothing found dated after 11-11): memory names fell about 26% from the 10-29 close to the 11-06 close, then bounced hard on 11-11 (MU reported up roughly 7-11%) after Morgan Stanley said the valuation pullback had improved risk-reward for memory, while DRAM contract pricing is still described as rising. The 25% MU leg re-entered on 11-09 is +6.2% and is doing what it was bought to do. Goldman preferring SK hynix and Samsung over MU, plus a single-day rebound that has not been confirmed, are not enough to resize yet. I keep the 75% cash at 4% until the post-rout tape shows a higher low, and keep the -20% stop and +45% take-profit. Trading now would only add churn costs with no new edge.
